prompts.text: What's the first thing you would want to learn if you could take one lesson from a musician you admire?
Tell me about somebody practising a piece of music until you finally heard it begin to come together.
You have a week to prepare one short performance on an unfamiliar instrument. How would you use your first hour?
Practising music is as much about noticing small differences as repeating the same passage.
Learning to play one complete simple song or understanding several useful musical patterns you could build on?
A musician's slow practice can sound very different from their final performance.
How can you tell whether a musician is practising for accuracy or exploring different ways to express something?
A beginner feels discouraged because their first recording sounds awkward. What would you help them listen for?
Describe an experience where someone else's dedication to practising made you appreciate their performance more.
What do you think makes a practice routine enjoyable enough to keep returning to?
How could live performances become more enjoyable for people with different hearing or sensory needs?
Tell me about an accessible performance or creative format that changed your understanding of who can participate in music.
You're designing a community music event for people with very different abilities. Who would you consult before choosing the programme?
Making music more accessible often leads to creative ideas that benefit everyone.
Exploring the vibration of low musical sounds or learning how visual cues can help people follow a performance?
People can experience musical rhythm through movement and vibration as well as through sound.
What would you ask a performer who creates music using adaptive instruments or technology?
A venue wants to offer a quiet listening space alongside a lively concert area. What should it consider?
Describe a time a different presentation of an artwork helped you notice something you'd missed.
How might the design of a concert space affect whether different listeners feel welcome?
What song from your childhood do you remember because of a story or game connected to it?
Tell me about a musical game you learned as a child that you could probably still demonstrate today.
You have to introduce a group of children to rhythm without any instruments. What activity would you try?
Early musical experiences can shape curiosity even when someone never studies music formally.
A storybook with little musical themes for its characters or a playground game built around call-and-response singing?
Children often treat singing, talking and making rhythmic sounds as parts of the same activity.
What would you want children to understand about music before teaching them to read notes?
A child asks why a sad song can still be beautiful. How would you start that conversation?
Describe a time you saw somebody discover the joy of making music for the first time.
Why do you think certain childhood melodies remain easy to remember after many years?
Have you heard an electronic sound in music that seemed unlike any traditional instrument?
Tell me about discovering how a familiar synth sound was originally made.
You have a synthesiser with only three controls. What change would you experiment with first?
Electronic music can be deeply expressive even when none of its sounds imitate acoustic instruments.
Exploring soft, slowly changing synthesiser textures or sharp rhythmic sounds that feel almost percussive?
A simple electronic tone can seem warm, metallic or distant depending on how it changes over time.
What would you like a sound designer to explain about shaping a tone from its very beginning?
A composer wants a sound that suggests curiosity without using a recognisable instrument. Where might they start?
Describe a piece of electronic music that made you imagine a physical place or object.
How much of the appeal of an unfamiliar electronic sound comes from not knowing what produced it?
What musical pattern would you be curious to understand through numbers or geometry?
Tell me about discovering that something you enjoyed in music had a surprisingly clear underlying pattern.
A friend wants you to show how fractions relate to rhythm using only claps. How would you begin?
Understanding musical patterns can deepen enjoyment without making listening feel like solving a problem.
Exploring how different rhythms fit together or seeing how a string's length changes its pitch?
A repeating pattern can sound entirely different when it starts at a new point in the musical phrase.
Have you ever noticed a song using an unusual number of beats without knowing the technical name for it?
Two drummers play patterns that repeat after different lengths. What would you listen for when they finally meet again?
Describe hearing a complicated rhythm become easier to follow once someone counted it out.
Where do you think mathematical structure leaves room for surprise in music?
Why do you think particular songs become inseparable from certain celebrations?
Tell me about a celebration where a song brought different generations onto the floor together.
You're choosing music for a community event with people from several backgrounds. What would you ask the organisers first?
Music can help an ordinary gathering feel ceremonial without requiring an elaborate setting.
A traditional performance that marks the beginning of an event or a lively shared song that closes it?
The same song can have a different meaning at a wedding, a school reunion and a farewell.
Have you ever noticed a community celebrating through music in a way you wanted to understand better?
An annual festival wants to introduce one new musical element without losing its identity. How might it choose?
Describe a moment when the timing of a song made a celebration unexpectedly emotional.
What makes music feel like a shared tradition rather than simply entertainment at an event?
Have you loved a song in a language you don't understand and later looked up what it meant?
Tell me about hearing the meaning of a translated lyric and being surprised by the story.
Two singers from different language backgrounds want to collaborate. What might help them preserve each other's musical identity?
A song can communicate something to listeners who don't understand its words without becoming culturally interchangeable.
Hearing a favourite melody sung in its original language or learning the story behind a carefully translated version?
The rhythms of spoken language often influence how a melody feels natural to sing.
What questions would you ask before trying to understand a traditional song from a culture unfamiliar to you?
A songwriter wants to adapt a chorus into another language while keeping its emotional meaning. What might be the hardest part?
Describe finding common ground with someone through music even though your preferred languages differed.
How do you think learning the meaning of a song changes your relationship with its sound?
Which two musical styles would you be curious to hear combined by artists who understand both?
Tell me about a collaboration that surprised you because the musicians seemed so different.
A jazz pianist and a traditional percussionist have one afternoon together. What might help them start creating?
A good cross-genre collaboration should create room for both musicians rather than using one as decoration.
A choir joining an electronic producer or an acoustic folk musician working with a beatmaker?
The most interesting collaborations can begin when artists disagree about which part of a song should come first.
Have you ever discovered a genre through a guest artist on a track you already liked?
Two musicians share a melody but interpret its rhythm differently. How could that difference become part of the arrangement?
Describe a musical partnership where the result sounded unlike either artist's solo work.
What tells you that artists in a collaboration are genuinely listening to one another?
Have you ever noticed a song finding a second life years after its original release?
Tell me about discovering that a soundtrack, dance trend or public event introduced new listeners to an older song.
An artist learns that their little-known song has become important at local celebrations abroad. What would you want to ask the community using it?
Listeners keep creating new meanings for songs long after the original recording is finished.
Hearing a forgotten track return through a film or discovering it in a friend's old playlist?
The moment a song becomes popular again can change how people talk about its original era.
What makes you interested in the history of a song that's suddenly appearing everywhere?
You can interview someone who first heard a song decades ago and a person who discovered it yesterday. What question would you ask both?
Describe an old recording you only encountered because somebody much younger shared it.
How do you think artists feel when audiences attach new stories to music they made long ago?
If you could ask an artist about one musical decision in a favourite track, what would you choose?
Tell me about an interview that made you hear a song differently afterwards.
You have five minutes with a musician just after a concert. What question would invite an answer beyond 'It was great'?
The most revealing questions for musicians often concern the choices they nearly made but didn't.
Asking a drummer how they developed a groove or asking a songwriter which lyric took the longest to finish?
An artist may remember the circumstances of recording a song more vividly than the final result.
What do you think fans most often misunderstand about the process of making music?
A musician says their most popular song was the easiest to finish. What would you want to know next?
Describe learning that a seemingly spontaneous performance required a surprising amount of preparation.
If you were making a short documentary about a musician, what part of their ordinary creative life would you want to show?
